title: Attended S=1 first-fill canary
description:
Run one attended live writer on a dedicated account containing only the canary
capital, one currently active operator-selected ticker, rung canary, and S=1.

The first post-adoption directional entry from acknowledgement, newly
classified owned fill, or complete-position fallback must durably latch
WINDING_DOWN. Demonstrate create visibility, structural post_only, complete
cancel sweep, correct fill attribution and backfilled provenance, zero taker
fees, one-sided aggregate-capped reduction, monitor and alert continuity, flat
completion, no new adding order, and restart that remains latched.

Acceptance: retain run ID, config hash, gate commit, order/fill IDs, transition
causes, anomaly and notification evidence, final exchange position, and restart
result. Every UNKNOWN is resolved, every SEV2 is dispositioned, no SEV1 occurs
except the expected canary stop cause, and the account ends flat and latched.
This bead does not authorise repeated cycles or S=12.
notes: PROCESS AUDIT 2026-09-26 (user-directed personal-project workflow): notes/verification-workflow.md and pilot-plan.md sections 5-6 supersede older universal full-catalogue and per-bead gate requirements. dependencies.title: Read-only qualification: 4-6h real process, zero writes
dependencies.description:
Run the real one-market process for a supervised 4–6 hour operating window with H-VER-1 unarmed. This is a read-only operational qualification, not the promotion gate for the later writer. It proves that the nominated commit can observe the real account, restart from its durable paths, remain monitored, and expose every attempted write without any network non-GET call.

Use the actual launchd/caffeinate supervision, five-record store, alert channel and external dead man. Force at least one websocket disconnect/quarantine/reconnect/resnapshot/reconcile and one process death/restart using the same durable paths. A safely forced event may discover and fail a missing relay; q01 does not require unrelated exchange write-response behavior to be implemented before the observer is allowed to run.

Owner-only stall and exchange schedule/host-clock jump remain deterministic promotion scenarios, not q01 live drills. The production binary has no safe external mechanism to freeze one goroutine or make the exchange change its schedule, and changing the host clock is not a defensible real-account test. q01 still exercises ordinary schedule polling and proves the real monitor/heartbeat paths continue.

Require at least 99% monitor availability against elapsed-time cadence, fresh complete position/order/fill walks, continuing heartbeat in every reached global state, bounded durable would-write and attempted-method evidence, and no silent anomaly loss. Preserve the compact qualification bundle.

No agent executes this bead against the real account. Live-account execution, forced external events and alarm confirmation are operator actions.
dependencies.acceptance_criteria:
Attach start/end timestamps, exact commit and config hash, actual transport method counts measured below the write guard, attempted methods measured above it, disconnect/reconnect/reconcile timestamps, state/anomaly summary, monitor/portfolio freshness evidence, committed-run restart linkage, bounded would-write episodes, heartbeat/dead-man check-in evidence, and proof that the external missed-heartbeat alarm fired.

The assessor requires at least four hours of linked monotonic active time; the operator plans an orderly end by six hours. Running long does not retroactively falsify safety evidence, so six hours is an operating cutoff rather than a qualification loophole or a machine failure condition. Any network non-GET call, unexplained SEV1, anomaly-drop evidence, cadence-adjusted monitor ratio below 99%, incomplete/stale portfolio coverage, missed heartbeat, incomplete adoption/reconciliation, corrupt evidence bundle, unlinked segment, or unbounded local reservation/evidence growth fails qualification. Before starting, verify the composed two-key write guard, applicable current read contracts and relevant local test/safety evidence under notes/verification-workflow.md. A complete mutation-catalogue run and unrelated writer-feature completion are not observer-entry prerequisites.
dependencies.notes:
Candidate identity for the q01 attempt (prepared 2026-08-12, not yet started).

  nominated commit  dc77e3f  (the commit lip-jy4 closed GREEN, 273/273)
  binary            /Users/hugh/.lip/bin/harness
  binary sha256     1882b82fbec9c00aeb683086fb2d1e11a86cbcd7fff0462b96dfba3fdd8d0cf1
  built from        /Users/hugh/kek/lip-q01-build/go  (detached worktree at
                    dc77e3f, tree verified clean at build time)
  toolchain         go1.26.4
  config            /Users/hugh/.lip/canary/config.json
  ticker            KXMAMDANIMENTION-26AUG12-SAFE
  evidence bundle   /Users/hugh/.lip/canary/q01-evidence.json
  launchd label     com.lip.harness
  runbook           /Users/hugh/.lip/q01-runbook.md

BINARY IDENTITY IS THE SHA256 ALONE. This repo's module lives in go/ while the
git root is one level up, and under that layout Go emits no vcs.revision /
vcs.modified build setting even when -buildvcs=true is passed explicitly --
verified, no error and no stamp. So currentBinaryIdentity()
(cmd/harness/qualification.go:144) appends nothing to the hash. Two consequences
worth recording here rather than rediscovering later:

  - The dirty working tree at build time (.beads/interactions.jsonl modified,
    .codex-handoff/ untracked) could not have contaminated the evidence bundle.
    That risk does not exist under this layout.
  - The commit linkage is an operator assertion, not a self-attestation by the
    binary -- but it is checkable, because the build is deterministic. Checking
    out dc77e3f to /Users/hugh/kek/lip-q01-build and running
    `go build -o <out> ./cmd/harness` from go/ under go1.26.4 reproduces
    1882b82f... byte for byte; two independent builds already did. The path
    matters: without -trimpath the build directory is embedded.

CONFIG. Byte-identical to the reviewed config.example.json apart from `ticker`,
so the template's "a diff of the file against an empty one is the whole config
review" property holds. s=1 canary, so no -rung flag is required (main.go:370).

TICKER SELECTION. The active LIP universe is 3,245 markets across 4 pages.
score.py, q1select.py and the lip.db collector all read ONE page of 200 with no
cursor, so every view built on them is truncated; cmd/harness does a complete
cursor walk (harness/rest/read.go:630) and refuses to start on a ticker outside
the complete set. Membership was therefore re-tested against the complete walk,
which KXMAMDANIMENTION-26AUG12-SAFE passes. A lip.db-based reading that showed
this ticker present in only 17 of 61 recent snapshots was a paging artifact, not
a membership lapse.

The hazard the choice is made against is a programme lapsing ACROSS THE MANDATED
RESTART DRILL: every restart re-runs the active-programme walk, and a ticker that
has fallen out by then turns KeepAlive:true into a respawn loop against a start
refusal, with the run dead and nothing reporting it. This ticker's programme end
and market close are both 2026-09-03T14:00Z -- 22 days of runway, so neither can
fire inside a 4-6h window. Book traffic is not a qualification risk: the monitor
ticks at 1 Hz unconditionally (cmd/harness/monitor.go:65), so slot freshness
comes from the harness's own cadence and not from market activity.

TWO OPERATING TRAPS recorded before the run rather than after:

  - The restart drill must SIGKILL the harness CHILD, by pid. The launchd job's
    argv is `/usr/bin/caffeinate -is <harness> ...`
    (harness/lifecycle/launchd.go:125), so caffeinate is the process launchd
    tracks and harness is its child. `pkill -f harness` matches both, and
    SIGKILLing caffeinate orphans a still-running harness while launchd starts a
    second one, which the instance lock then refuses in a respawn loop. SIGTERM
    is also wrong: it sets WINDING_DOWN and commits a durable stop
    (main.go:300-307), which would make the rest of the window a wind-down
    rather than an observation.
  - paths.stop cannot end the run. It is Section 12's out-of-band halt and
    explicitly not a drain (config.go:148-161): it stops the harness adding and
    can never end the process. The orderly end is
    `launchctl bootout gui/501/com.lip.harness`.

Editing the config or rebuilding the binary between deploy and assessment makes
every restart fail with ErrMetadataMismatch (harness/qual/recorder.go:307),
which under KeepAlive is a silent respawn loop. Nothing changes mid-run.

Start was blocked by lip-83o: LaunchdPlan.Render() writes booleans as <true></true> and launchd rejects that form with 'Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error', so -deploy's plist has never been loadable. Isolated by single-variable probe agents; only the tag form predicts the failure. Working around it operator-side in ~/.lip/q01.sh, which runs plutil -convert xml1 over the installed plist before bootstrapping and asserts no paired booleans remain. The conversion is semantics-preserving -- ProgramArguments verified byte-identical across it -- so the deployed argv is still exactly what installAgent wrote, and the run's identity is unaffected. No Go was edited, so the mutation catalogue that closed lip-jy4 against dc77e3f still holds.
ATTEMPT 1 ABORTED 2026-08-12T17:33Z after ~3 minutes, on lip-9tr. Portfolio slots read observed 12 / fresh_complete 0 / incomplete_walks 12 while monitor slots were a clean 60/60, so the local bar was already unreachable and six hours would only have produced a guaranteed failure. Cause is real exchange data: fill 1582884a-1f64-7c20-fab4-b40468ad5df6 carries fee_cost "0.017200", six decimals, and portfolio.go:564 parses fee_cost with rest.ParsePrice4, whose measured quantum is 1e-4 dollars. convertFills errors, FILL_UNCONVERTIBLE SEV1 fires, the whole walk is discarded and the fills freshness clock does not advance -- once per 5s poll, permanently, because the fill is historical and appears in every complete walk. No operational workaround exists. The alert path worked correctly throughout: the SEV1 was delivered to the operator's phone with urgent priority within seconds, alongside the STARTUP summary and a SEV2 RESNAPSHOT_DEFERRED.

dependencies.title: EPIC CR-1: one-market continuous runtime
dependencies.description:
CR-1 means one operator-selected active-program market at S=12 may repeat
maker-entry, reduction, flat and requote cycles without synchronous operator
involvement during one declared market assignment. It runs under launchd and
caffeinate, survives process and websocket restarts through safe adoption, and
either continues safely or durably enters WINDING_DOWN while reduction,
monitoring, heartbeat and alert retry remain alive.

The closed operating envelope is: one selected ticker; dedicated account with
only declared capital and no unrelated cash, positions, orders or manual
activity; manual market replacement; no claim of automatic programme rotation.
Required evidence is a green read-only qualification, clean S=1 first-fill
canary, clean attended S=12 burn-in, final scenario/invariant and operational
readiness, exact full promotion gate, active external dead man, and explicit
operator review.

New work blocks CR-1 only after adjudication that its failure is reachable in
this operating envelope or that CR-1 acceptance cannot be evidenced without it.
Priority labels alone do not move the finish line. Dynamic selection, rotation
and automatic management of unrelated held markets belong to CR-2; CR-1 instead
refuses a dirty account and stops on foreign activity.

Acceptance: record exact commit, config/rung, assignment window, dedicated-
account check, supervision state, runbook/drill evidence and links to all three
promotion rungs. After closure, repeated cycles are authorised only inside that
assignment.
